title_en: Zhao Jinrong, Xu Zhiguo, Zhao Yongqiang, and Liu Shuhong — case of dereliction of duty, disclosing state secrets, and illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel
keywords_en: criminal; dereliction of duty; disclosure of state secrets; illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel; first instance; second instance; intermediate people's court; high people's court; Hebei Province; natural person; Criminal Law; Law on Guarding State Secrets; whether constitutes the crime of dereliction of duty; whether constitutes the crime of disclosing state secrets; whether constitutes the crime of illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel; affirmation of original judgment; standby letter of credit; introducing foreign investment; disclosure of meeting secrets; guarantee
full_text_en:
Zhao Jinrong, Xu Zhiguo, Zhao Yongqiang, Liu Shuhong — dereliction of duty, leaking state secrets, and illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel

Defendant Zhao Jinrong, male, 53 years old, former president of the Hengshui Central Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Hebei Province, arrested on June 13, 1993.

Defendant Xu Zhiguo, male, 47 years old, former vice president of the Hengshui Central Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Hebei Province, arrested on June 13, 1993.

Defendant Zhao Yongqiang, male, 30 years old, former English teacher at Hengshui Normal College, Hebei Province, arrested on July 27, 1993.

Defendant Liu Shuhong, female, 34 years old, former deputy section chief of the Foreign Exchange Business Section of the Hengshui Central Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Hebei Province, arrested on April 1, 1994.

The Hengshui Branch of Hebei Provincial People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution with the Hengshui Intermediate People's Court against defendant Zhao Jinrong for crimes of dereliction of duty and leaking state secrets, defendant Xu Zhiguo for crimes of dereliction of duty and illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel, defendant Zhao Yongqiang for the crime of illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel, and defendant Liu Shuhong for the crime of dereliction of duty.

After trial, the Hengshui Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

At the end of March 1993, defendants Zhao Jinrong and Xu Zhiguo met with Americans Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming (separately dealt with) in Hengshui City, Hebei Province, to discuss cooperation in introducing foreign funds. Zhao Jinrong and Xu Zhiguo believed the lies fabricated by Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming that only by issuing standby letters of credit as formalities from the Hengshui Central Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as the Hengshui Agricultural Bank) could they introduce huge sums of funds from the international financial market for the Hengshui Agricultural Bank, and that the Hengshui Agricultural Bank would not need to repay the principal or interest on the introduced funds, nor bear any liability for the letters of credit issued. Without understanding the letter of credit business or the creditworthiness of Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming, and without collective discussion and decision by the bank's leadership, nor truthful reporting to the local government or higher-level bank, they, on April 1-2 of the same year, signed an agreement on behalf of the Hengshui Agricultural Bank to introduce foreign funds of USD 10 billion. On April 4, Zhao Jinrong sent Xu Zhiguo to the Agricultural Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as the Head Office of Agricultural Bank) to consult on the feasibility of introducing foreign funds. Without consulting the International Business Department, which was in charge of foreign exchange business, at the Head Office of Agricultural Bank, Xu Zhiguo returned to Hengshui and told Zhao Jinrong: "The Head Office of Agricultural Bank thinks that introducing foreign funds is a good thing," prompting Zhao Jinrong to decide to proceed with the matter. On April 5, without Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming providing the counter-guarantee as previously promised, Zhao Jinrong and Xu Zhiguo, exceeding the bank's business scope, issued 200 standby letters of credit totaling USD 10 billion. Zhao Jinrong and defendant Liu Shuhong signed their respective names on the letters of credit according to their duties, then handed them over to Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming to be sent abroad. On April 7, the Hengshui Agricultural Bank received an inquiry from a foreign enterprise regarding the standby letters of credit issued. Zhao Jinrong and Liu Shuhong signed a telex unconditionally confirming the standby letters of credit, drafted by Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming, and replied to the inquiry. On April 15, Zhao Jinrong, at the request of Mei Zhifang, together with Liu Shuhong, issued a reply to an inquiry from another foreign enterprise. On April 17, the Hebei Provincial Agricultural Bank requested Zhao Jinrong and Xu Zhiguo to report on the issuance of the standby letters of credit. To conceal their dereliction of duty, Zhao Jinrong and Xu Zhiguo asked Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming for the counter-guarantee letter they had previously promised. Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming then fabricated a standby letter of credit for USD 10 billion from the "United Nations Republic Bank." Zhao Jinrong, knowing that this letter of credit was invalid, still submitted it to the higher-level bank. On April 21, a Hong Kong enterprise sent an inquiry letter. Zhao Jinrong and Liu Shuhong, although already criticized by the higher-level bank's responsible person for unauthorized issuance of letters of credit, still signed a reply unconditionally confirming the standby letters of credit. After the standby letters of credit from the Hengshui Agricultural Bank were sent abroad, they were directly sold. The Head Office of Agricultural Bank suffered huge economic losses in pursuing these letters of credit, and its financial reputation was also severely damaged.

On May 26, 1993, defendant Zhao Jinrong attended a meeting of the Head Office of Agricultural Bank deciding to report to the public security organs for investigation of the fraudulent activities of Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming (hereinafter referred to as the "5.26" meeting). Zhao Jinrong, knowing that the content of the meeting was a secret matter concerning major national interests and having been specifically instructed by relevant leaders to keep it confidential, still disclosed the content of the meeting to defendant Xu Zhiguo. To enable Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming to escape and to facilitate the concealment of his own dereliction of duty, Xu Zhiguo wrote the above secret matters on a note and handed it to defendant Zhao Yongqiang, who was employed by the Hengshui Agricultural Bank as an interpreter, to inform Mei Zhifang. At the same time, Zhao Yongqiang also informed Mei Zhifang of the telex that the Hengshui Agricultural Bank intended to send to relevant overseas enterprises to revoke the standby letters of credit in order to mitigate losses. Zhao Yongqiang sent this telex to another address provided by Mei Zhifang, thereby undermining the Hengshui Agricultural Bank's measures to eliminate the risk of the standby letters of credit.

The Hengshui Intermediate People's Court held: The "Measures for the Administration of Foreign Exchange Guarantees Provided by Domestic Institutions" issued by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange stipulate that foreign exchange guarantees provided to overseas institutions shall be subject to the approval of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. The sample authorized signatures published by the Head Office of Agricultural Bank did not include the signatures of defendants Zhao Jinrong and Liu Shuhong. Moreover, the business license of the International Business Agency of the Hengshui Agricultural Bank did not include international settlement or foreign exchange guarantee business. Zhao Jinrong, as president of the Hengshui Agricultural Bank, failed to perform his duties, believed the lies of Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming, violated industry management regulations, and issued standby letters of credit totaling USD 10 billion without authorization, severely damaging the property rights and financial reputation of the Agricultural Bank of China and causing significant losses to state interests. His conduct constituted the crime of dereliction of duty as provided in Article 187 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and should be severely punished according to law. The "5.26" meeting discussed matters such as reporting to the public security organs and investigating the fraudulent crimes of Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming. Pursuant to Article 8, paragraph (6) of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Guarding State Secrets, such matters constitute state secrets, and participants had the duty to maintain confidentiality. Zhao Jinrong violated confidentiality regulations by leaking the secret matters of the "5.26" meeting, and the circumstances were serious. His conduct constituted the crime of leaking state secrets as provided in Article 186 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and should be punished according to law. Zhao Jinrong committed multiple crimes and should be subjected to combined punishment for multiple crimes pursuant to Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Defendant Xu Zhiguo, as vice president, failed to perform his duties in charge of foreign exchange business. After believing the lies of Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming, he played an important role in the bank's violation of industry management regulations and unauthorized issuance of standby letters of credit totaling USD 10 billion, causing significant losses to state interests. His conduct constituted the crime of dereliction of duty as provided in Article 187 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and should be severely punished according to law. Xu Zhiguo, knowing that the content of the "5.26" meeting was a secret matter concerning major national interests, illegally provided it to Mei Zhifang to facilitate their escape. His conduct constituted the crime of illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel as provided in the "Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Punishment of Crimes of Leaking State Secrets," and the circumstances of the crime were particularly serious. He should be severely punished according to law. Xu Zhiguo committed multiple crimes and should be subjected to combined punishment for multiple crimes pursuant to Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Defendant Zhao Yongqiang actively participated in illegally providing the secret matters of the "5.26" meeting to Mei Zhifang and disclosed information about the Hengshui Agricultural Bank's intention to eliminate the risk of the letters of credit, thereby undermining the remedial measures. His conduct constituted the crime of illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel as provided in the "Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Punishment of Crimes of Leaking State Secrets," and the circumstances of the crime were particularly serious. He should be severely punished according to law.

Defendant Liu Shuhong failed to perform her duties as deputy section chief of the Foreign Exchange Business Section of the Hengshui Agricultural Bank, violated industry management regulations, participated in signing the standby letters of credit, and after being criticized by the higher-level bank, did not reform but continued to participate in signing the confirmation letters for the standby letters of credit. Her conduct constituted the crime of dereliction of duty as provided in Article 187 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Accordingly, on April 26, 1994, the Hengshui Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

Defendant Zhao Jinrong was sentenced to five years' imprisonment for the crime of dereliction of duty; to seven years' imprisonment and deprivation of political rights for two years for the crime of leaking state secrets; and the combined sentence was fixed at eleven years' imprisonment and deprivation of political rights for two years.

Defendant Xu Zhiguo was sentenced to five years' imprisonment for the crime of dereliction of duty; to fifteen years' imprisonment and deprivation of political rights for three years for the crime of illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel; and the combined sentence was fixed at nineteen years' imprisonment and deprivation of political rights for three years.

Defendant Zhao Yongqiang was sentenced to fourteen years' imprisonment and deprivation of political rights for three years for the crime of illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel.

Defendant Liu Shuhong was sentenced to one year's imprisonment for the crime of dereliction of duty.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, defendants Zhao Jinrong, Xu Zhiguo, Zhao Yongqiang, and Liu Shuhong refused to accept it and appealed to the Hebei High People's Court. Zhao Jinrong's grounds for appeal were: he did not exceed his authority in issuing the standby letters of credit; he did not know that the content of the "5.26" meeting was a state secret; and he did not constitute the crimes of dereliction of duty or leaking state secrets. Xu Zhiguo's grounds for appeal were: the circumstances of dereliction of duty were not serious, and the first instance sentence was too heavy; he did not know that the content of the "5.26" meeting was a state secret, and he did not constitute the crime of illegally providing state secrets to overseas personnel. Zhao Yongqiang's grounds for appeal were: he provided the content of the "5.26" meeting to Mei Zhifang in accordance with the instructions of the Hengshui Agricultural Bank leadership; he did not know that the content provided was a state secret; and the first instance sentence was too heavy. Liu Shuhong's grounds for appeal were: she signed the relevant documents under orders and did not know the nature and content of the documents, and therefore did not constitute a crime.

After trial, the Hebei High People's Court held: Appellant Zhao Jinrong was not an authorized signatory for letters of credit within the banking system, and the Hengshui Agricultural Bank did not have a letter of credit business; at the "5.26" meeting, relevant leaders informed Zhao Jinrong that the meeting content must be kept absolutely confidential, and after the meeting, relevant leaders specifically instructed him not to disclose the meeting content to Xu Zhiguo, yet Zhao Jinrong acted conversely, thus his grounds for appeal are not valid. Appellant Xu Zhiguo neglected his duties, was extremely irresponsible when consulting with the Head Office of Agricultural Bank about introducing funds, and played an important role in the Hengshui Agricultural Bank's reckless issuance of standby letters of credit; Xu Zhiguo also deliberately provided matters he knew should be kept confidential to Mei Zhifang, thus his grounds for appeal are not valid. Appellant Zhao Yongqiang knew that the content of the "5.26" meeting concerned major national interests and constituted a state secret, yet actively provided it to Mei Zhifang, undermining the Hengshui Agricultural Bank's measures to eliminate the risk of the letters of credit, thus his grounds for appeal cannot be sustained. Appellant Liu Shuhong was informed by Zhao Jinrong of the nature of the documents when she signed the standby letters of credit, and the last confirmation letter she signed was in Chinese, thus her grounds for appeal cannot be sustained either. The facts of the crimes committed by each defendant as determined in the first instance judgment are clear, the evidence is confirmed and sufficient, the conviction is accurate, the sentence is appropriate, and the trial procedure is lawful. Accordingly, on May 13, 1994, the Hebei High People's Court, pursuant to Article 136, paragraph (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a final ruling rejecting the appeals and affirming the original judgment.
